query_text: Need a profile editor app for my phone where the birthday and demographic fields each have their own little privacy toggle right next to them — so I can show my age to some people but hide my gender, or the other way around, all independently. The whole thing should feel soft and clean, like a well-designed personal card, where each field has its own little lock icon or eye icon you tap to decide who can see it. I want it to feel intentional and considered, not like a cluttered settings dump.

Payment and billing address update experience for a mobile app that feels reassuringly calm and trustworthy — like a well-designed bank app — where you tap to edit your card details or billing address and the whole flow guides you through one step at a time with a quiet, confident visual style. Each step should feel distinct, with subtle confirmation cues so you always know your info was saved properly and nothing slipped through.

Need a file uploader tool for my phone that actually handles bad connections properly — so if my wifi drops mid-upload it automatically tries again and picks up from where it left off instead of making me start the whole thing over from scratch. I lose so much time restarting failed uploads and it's exhausting, especially for bigger files. The app should show me clearly where the upload stopped and let me know when it successfully resumes so I'm not left guessing.

Need a file upload tool for my phone that can handle really big files without just sitting there looking frozen — I want to actually see what percentage is done and roughly how many minutes are left, so I know whether to wait or go do something else. Right now I upload stuff and have no idea if it's stuck or just slow, and it drives me crazy. The app should break big files into pieces quietly in the background and keep me updated the whole time so I'm never left staring at a spinning circle.

Create a file transfer tool for my phone that lets me send files to another device by scanning a QR code — so instead of fiddling with cables or trying to remember device names, I just open the app, pick the file I want to send, and a QR code appears that the other device scans to grab it instantly over the local connection. It should work fast and be simple enough that I can hand my phone to someone and they immediately understand how it works.

Build a document export tool for my phone that lets me save things as a PDF and actually choose whether I want it portrait or landscape, and set how much white space is around the edges before it saves — because right now everything just exports in whatever default settings and half the time stuff gets cut off or looks weirdly cramped. The app should let me preview what the PDF will look like with my chosen settings before I confirm and download it.

Build a file downloader tool for my phone where after a download finishes, it asks me what I actually want to do with the file — open it in a specific app right now, or save it to my files to deal with later — instead of just dumping it somewhere I have to go hunt for. It's so annoying to download something and then spend five minutes trying to find where it went. A simple choice right after the download completes would save me so much hassle every single time.

A download picker tool for my phone where I can go into a collection of files — like a photo album or a course pack — and check off only the specific ones I want to save, and before I hit download it tells me the total size so I know if it's going to eat up my storage or burn through my data. Right now it's all-or-nothing with no size warning and I keep running out of space because I accidentally grab way more than I needed. The mobile app should make selecting and previewing the total size really quick and obvious.

A download manager tool for my phone that actually lets me control what's happening — pause a download when I'm about to lose wifi, come back later and resume it, and see everything waiting in a queue so I know what's next. Right now downloads either fail silently or I have no idea what's going on, and if something interrupts it I have to start over completely. The mobile app should show each download's progress clearly and let me drag things around in the queue if I want something to go first.

Make a travel content manager for my phone that lets me download everything I need — maps, guides, saved articles — as one package before I leave, so I can use it all offline when I'm somewhere with bad data or roaming is too expensive. I hate getting somewhere and realizing I can't access anything because there's no signal. The app should let me pick which content packs to grab, show me how big each one is, and let me know when everything is ready to use offline.

Build a link sharing tool for my phone where I can grab the deep link to any piece of content and it automatically adds my tracking info — like a source label and campaign tag — to the end of the URL before copying it to my clipboard. I share links all the time across different places and I always forget to manually add the tracking bits, so I end up with no idea where my traffic actually came from. The app should let me set up my tracking tags once and then just one tap copies the full ready-to-share link.

Make a playlist manager for my phone where I can take an existing playlist I like and duplicate it with one tap, then rename the copy for a new season or mood — so I keep the original safe and can tweak the copy however I want. I rebuild the same playlists over and over every few months and it wastes so much time. The app should let me long-press or swipe on any playlist to clone it, and immediately drop me into a rename field so I can label it before it gets lost in the list.

Create a form builder tool for my phone that lets me take a form I've already set up — with all its questions, options, and field types — and instantly copy the whole structure into a new blank form, so all the fields come along exactly as they were and I just swap in new content. Rebuilding the same survey layout from scratch every time is such a waste, and I always mess up a field or two when I do it manually. The app should make cloning any existing form a one-tap thing right from the main list.

Need a spreadsheet tool for my phone where I can write a formula in one cell and then easily copy it across a whole row or column range in one go — so it adjusts itself for each column automatically and I'm not manually tapping and pasting into every single cell one by one. That part of working on spreadsheets on my phone takes forever right now. I just want to select the range I need, say copy formula across, and have it done instantly with the right values in each spot.

A habit tracker app for my phone where I can take a habit plan I finished — say a 30-day challenge — and duplicate it to kick off a fresh tracking period, so all my habits carry over and I just set a new start date rather than rebuilding everything from scratch every single time a cycle ends. I put effort into setting up my habits and I really hate losing that work when a period is over. The mobile app should make it feel like flipping to a clean new page while keeping all my habits ready to go.

Build a workout planner for my phone where I can take a training plan I built for myself and copy it over to a different person's profile — like my workout buddy or a friend I'm coaching — so they get the exact same exercises, sets, and schedule without me having to type it all in again from scratch. Doing it manually for each person is just too tedious and I always make small mistakes. The mobile app should let me pick any existing plan and assign a copy of it to another profile in just a couple of taps.

Need a shopping and delivery manager for my phone that lets me tap a delivery address from any past order and save it straight to my address book with one tap, so I never have to type out the same address again next time I order to that place. Right now I dig through old orders just to copy-paste an address and it's such an unnecessary hassle. The mobile app should show a clear save-to-address-book option right on the order details so grabbing a delivery address is instant.

Build a report builder for my phone where I can take a report layout I've already set up and make a copy of it that stays connected to the same underlying information — so the duplicate pulls in the same data automatically and I can tweak how it looks or what it focuses on without messing with the original. I keep having to rebuild the same report structures for different purposes and it eats up way too much of my time. The mobile app should let me clone any report in one tap and immediately start customizing the copy.

Need a little helper tool for my phone where I can add small pop-up tip bubbles to any part of my app or page — so when someone taps a question mark or hovers near something confusing, a short helpful explanation pops up right there explaining what that thing does. I'm building a small tool for my team and people keep messaging me asking what certain buttons or fields mean. The mobile app should let me attach custom tip text to specific spots on the screen and control when those little bubbles appear and disappear.

Create a small engagement tool for my phone that keeps track of how much someone has used the app and then pops up a friendly rating nudge at a meaningful moment — like after they've completed their tenth task or used it for a week straight — rather than just randomly or on first launch. I'm making a little productivity tool and I want people to feel the ask is earned, not intrusive. The mobile app should let me set which milestones trigger the rating prompt and make the pop-up feel warm and casual.

Create a guided tour tool for my phone where new users get a spotlight that dims everything else and draws attention to one thing at a time — like a highlighted circle around a button with a short note explaining what it's for — so people can learn the app by actually seeing and tapping through it rather than reading a wall of help text. I'm making a small tool for people who aren't very tech-savvy and I want them to feel walked through it on their first use. The mobile app should let me set the order of the spotlight steps and let users tap through at their own pace.

Make a goal tracker for my phone that bursts into a fun confetti animation whenever someone hits a milestone — like finishing a challenge or reaching a streak — and then immediately gives them an easy way to share that moment with friends right there while the feeling is fresh. I'm putting together a little personal wins tracker and I want completing something to actually feel like a celebration, not just a checkbox going grey. The mobile app should make the confetti pop feel lively and the share option obvious so people actually use it.

Need a multi-account manager for my phone that lets me flip between different accounts — like a personal one and a work one — with just a quick tap, so I stay logged in to both and can switch instantly without going through a whole sign-out and sign-in cycle every time. I use the same tool for work and personal stuff and constantly logging out to switch is genuinely annoying. The mobile app should show all my saved accounts in one place and switching should feel instant, like flipping between tabs.

Build a notification manager for my phone where tapping a push notification actually takes me straight to the exact piece of content it's about — a specific message, a task, a post — instead of just opening the app to the home screen and making me hunt for whatever triggered the alert. I miss the point of notifications half the time because they drop me in the wrong place. The mobile app should handle each notification type and land me directly on the right spot every single time I tap one.

Need a task manager for my phone where after I delete something by accident, a little message pops up at the bottom of the screen with an undo button and a countdown — like five seconds — so I can catch my mistake and tap undo before it's gone forever, instead of just losing it immediately with no chance to recover. I delete the wrong thing way too often and then have to recreate it from scratch. The mobile app should show the undo countdown clearly so I actually have time to react if I need to.
